mainTopic: Ranking the four death penalties, and the law of a בת כהן who sins
overview: This amud finishes ranking the four court death penalties: סקילה, שריפה, חנק and סייף. The גמרא shows that סקילה is harsher than חנק, because the Torah moved a betrothed girl from the married woman's חנק to סקילה. It then shows that סקילה and חנק are each harsher than סייף. In both cases the proof is that the מדיח who leads a city astray is worse than the people he misleads, who get סייף. Next comes רבי יוחנן's favorite ברייתא, where the רבנן and רבי שמעון argue over a betrothed בת כהן who sinned. The argument turns on whether סקילה or שריפה is harsher, which also matters for someone who earned two court deaths. רבי שמעון proves that שריפה is harsher, because one פסוק moves a בת כהן out of both the married group and the betrothed group. Finally, a ברייתא reads the פסוק of בת כהן word by word. It teaches that only sins of זנות count, only while she is tied to a husband, with any man, and at any age. The explanation of the words 'בת כהן' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The subverter's sin is worse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the מדיח, who leads others into idol worship, has the more severe sin. So, according to רבי שמעון who gives him חנק, his punishment (חנק) is harsher than the punishment of the people he led astray (סייף).
steps.simpleTranslation: You have to say: the subverter's power is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before this passage: who is worse, the one who leads a city into idol worship, or the people who follow him? It says the leader is worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, the people who led an עיר הנדחת astray get חנק, while the city's residents get סייף. Since the leader is clearly the worse sinner, his punishment, חנק, must be harsher than סייף. This is the step the קל וחומר that follows needs.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say, meaning this is the only sensible answer
Power or force; here it means the weight or severity of his sin
A subverter, someone who leads others to worship idols

phrases.english: You must say: the severity of the subverter [is greater].
phrases.notes: He means the leader who led the city astray is worse than the people who followed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes an argument that began before this passage, comparing the subverters and the subverted in an עיר הנדחת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מדיח is worse than those he subverts, so, according to רבי שמעון who gives the מדיח חנק, חנק is harsher than סייף.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: burning is harsher than the sword
steps.stepSummary: Using a קל וחומר, the גמרא proves that שריפה is harsher than סייף. If שריפה is harsher than חנק, and חנק is already harsher than סייף, then שריפה is certainly harsher than סייף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here is a קל וחומר: if strangulation, which is harsher than the sword, is still less harsh than burning, then the sword, which is the most lenient, is certainly less harsh than burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a logical proof that שריפה is harsher than סייף. It builds a ladder of severity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works like a chain: שריפה is above חנק, and חנק is above סייף. So שריפה must also be above סייף. חנק over סייף was just shown from the מדיח (who gets חנק according to רבי שמעון), and שריפה over חנק is already known.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a heavier one: if it is true there, it is surely true here
Strangulation, one of the four court death penalties
Death by the sword (beheading), the most lenient of the four
Burning, one of the four court death penalties
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: And [it follows] a fortiori:
if strangulation, which is more severe than the sword —
burning is more severe than it;
the sword, which is lenient — is it not all the more so?
phrases.notes: Finish the sentence in your head: burning is certainly harsher than the sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further logical proof about where סייף sits on the ladder of severity.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the known rankings: שריפה over חנק, and חנק over סייף.
steps.whatToRemember: סייף is the most lenient punishment: חנק is harsher than it (from the מדיח, according to רבי שמעון), and so is שריפה (from the קל וחומר).

steps.title: Claim: stoning is harsher than strangulation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new comparison and suggests that סקילה is harsher than חנק, because סקילה is given for מגדף and עבודה זרה. These sins attack the very core of the faith, as the גמרא said earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stoning is harsher than strangulation, since it is given to the blasphemer and to the idol worshipper. And why are those sins so severe? As we said before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new pair to rank, סקילה against חנק, and offers a first reason why סקילה is the harsher one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is to judge a punishment by the sins it is given for. מגדף and עבודה זרה strike at the foundation of belief in הקב״ה, so the punishment the Torah gives for them must be among the harshest.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, one of the four court death penalties
A blasphemer, one who curses הקב״ה's Name
Idol worship
Severity or stringency
As we said earlier

phrases.english: Stoning is more severe than strangulation,
since it is given to the blasphemer
and to one who worships idols.
And what is the severity? As we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier explanation: these sinners attack the very foundation of the faith.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from סייף and שריפה to a new comparison: סקילה versus חנק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סקילה is harsher than חנק because it is given for מגדף and עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Pushback: maybe strangulation is harsher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe חנק is harsher, since it is given to someone who hits his father or mother. Honoring parents is compared in the Torah to honoring הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: strangulation is harsher, since it is given to one who strikes his father or mother. And why is that so severe? Because it is compared to honoring הקב״ה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim of step 3 by using the very same method in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we rank punishments by the sins they are given for, חנק also has a strong case. Hitting a parent is linked in the Torah to disrespecting הקב״ה Himself. So this method alone cannot decide which punishment is harsher.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the opposite is true
One who strikes his father or mother
Was compared or linked by the Torah
Etc., short for the rest of a known phrase

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final view. The אדרבה shows that judging by the sins on both sides leads nowhere, so a different kind of proof is needed in the next step.

phrases.english: On the contrary: strangulation is more severe,
since it is given to one who strikes his father and his mother.
And what is the severity? Since it is compared, etc.
phrases.notes: The full idea: honoring your parents is compared to honoring הקב״ה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reasoning as step 3 to argue the opposite conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 3 that סקילה is harsher than חנק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנק is also given for a sin linked to honoring הקב״ה (hitting a parent), so judging by the sins does not prove סקילה is harsher.

steps.title: Proof from the betrothed girl: stoning is harsher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the question. The Torah took a betrothed girl (ארוסה) out of the rule for a married woman (נשואה), whose punishment is חנק, and gave her סקילה instead. This shows that סקילה is the harsher punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah took the betrothed Jewish girl out of the category of the married Jewish woman, changing her punishment from strangulation to stoning, we learn from this that stoning is harsher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback with a stronger proof that does not depend on comparing sins. It concludes that סקילה is harsher than חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married woman who commits adultery gets חנק, but a betrothed girl who does the same gets סקילה. When the Torah singles out one case from a general group and changes its punishment, the change is a step up in strictness. So סקילה ranks above חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (literally, the Merciful One) took it out
A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before נישואין
A fully married woman
The daughter of a regular Jew, not of a כהן
Learn from this; conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: סקילה is harsher than חנק. The proof is that the Torah moved the ארוסה out of the married woman's חנק and into סקילה, not the comparison of which sins each punishment covers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This method, seeing where the Torah moves a case out of its usual group, gives a reliable way to rank punishments when comparing the sins themselves ends in a tie.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One took out the betrothed daughter of a Yisrael
from the category of a married daughter of a Yisrael
from strangulation to stoning,
conclude from it: stoning is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the tie created by the אדרבה in step 4 with a proof based on the Torah moving a case from one punishment to another.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New, decisive proof that replaces the tied comparison of sins
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Judging by the sins, חנק could be harsher, since it is given for hitting a parent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the Torah moved the ארוסה from חנק to סקילה, סקילה is the harsher punishment.

steps.title: Stoning is harsher than the sword
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא claims that סקילה is harsher than סייף, because סקילה is given for מגדף and עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stoning is more severe than the sword, since it is given to the blasphemer, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new comparison: סקילה against סייף. It uses the same reason it gave before, that סקילה punishes sins that attack the faith itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא compared סקילה with חנק. Now it compares סקילה with סייף. The reasoning is the same: the sins punished with סקילה, מגדף and עבודה זרה, are the most serious.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by the sword (beheading)
One who curses ה׳ (a blasphemer)
Short for 'and so on'; the list continues as before

phrases.english: Stoning is more severe than the sword,
since it is given to the blasphemer, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points back to the full reason from before: it is also given to someone who worships idols.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning from step 3 for a new pair: סקילה against סייף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סקילה is harsher than סייף because it punishes מגדף and עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Maybe the sword is harsher, because of the city led astray
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe סייף is harsher, since the people of an עיר הנדחת get סייף and also lose their property.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: the sword is more severe, since it is given to the people of a city led astray. And what makes it more severe? Their property is destroyed too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 6. It suggests that סייף might be the harsher punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of an עיר הנדחת are killed by סייף, and their property is destroyed as well. That extra loss makes their punishment look harsher than an ordinary סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
A city whose people were led to worship idols
Their property is destroyed

phrases.english: On the contrary: the sword is more severe,
since it is given to the people of a city led astray.
And what is the severity?
Since their property is destroyed as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה: סַיִיף חָמוּר שֶׁכֵּן נִיתַּן לְאַנְשֵׁי עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ranking from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that סקילה is harsher than סייף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סייף punishes the people of an עיר הנדחת, and they also lose their property, so סייף may be the harsher penalty.

steps.title: The one who leads astray sinned worse
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the מדיח, who gets סקילה, sinned worse than the people he led astray, who get סייף. So סקילה is harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should say: whose sin carries more weight, the one who leads astray or the one who is led astray? You must say: the one who leads astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7. It compares the people who led the city astray with the people who followed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the עיר הנדחת case, the people who led the city astray get סקילה, and the people they led get סייף. The leader's sin is clearly worse, so the punishment he gets, סקילה, must be the harsher one.

keyTerms.meaning: One who leads others into idol worship
One who was led astray
You must say (the answer is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: The leader gets the harsher death. Since the מדיח gets סקילה and his followers get סייף, סקילה is harsher.

phrases.english: You should say: whose strength is greater,
phrases.notes: 'Strength' here means how heavy the sin is.

phrases.english: that of the one who leads astray, or that of the one led astray?
You must say: that of the one who leads astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses the challenger's own case against him: within the עיר הנדחת case, the worse sinner gets סקילה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing property makes the city people's סייף look harsher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מדיח sinned worse and gets סקילה, so סקילה is harsher than סייף.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: stoning beats the sword
steps.stepSummary: A second proof. If סקילה is harsher than חנק, and חנק is harsher than סייף, then סקילה is certainly harsher than סייף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is a קל וחומר: if strangulation, which is more severe than the sword, is still less severe than stoning, then surely the lighter sword is too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second proof, a קל וחומר, that סקילה is harsher than סייף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא already showed that סקילה is harsher than חנק. It treats חנק as harsher than סייף. If סקילה beats even חנק, it surely beats the lighter סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Death by strangulation
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: And there is a קל וחומר:
if strangulation, which is more severe than the sword,
still has stoning more severe than it,
then the lighter sword, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה חֶנֶק שֶׁחָמוּר מִסַּיִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof that supports the answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That סקילה is harsher than סייף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר built on step 5 (סקילה is harsher than חנק) and on חנק being harsher than סייף.

steps.title: Strangulation is harsher than the sword
steps.stepSummary: A new comparison: חנק is harsher than סייף, because it is given to someone who hits a parent, and honoring parents is compared to honoring הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Strangulation is more severe than the sword, since it is given to one who strikes his father or mother. And what makes it more severe? As we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next pair: חנק against סייף. It claims that חנק is harsher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר in step 9 treated חנק as harsher than סייף, and now the גמרא gives a reason for that. Hitting a parent gets חנק, and the Torah compares honoring parents to honoring הקב״ה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hits his father or mother
As we said (earlier)

phrases.english: Strangulation is more severe than the sword,
since it is given to one who strikes his father or his mother.
And what is the severity? As we said.
phrases.notes: Back in step 4: honoring parents is compared to honoring הקב״ה.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֶנֶק חָמוּר מִסַּיִיף, שֶׁכֵּן נִיתַּן לְמַכֵּה אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for the assumption used in step 9's קל וחומר (חנק is harsher than סייף).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנק is harsher than סייף because it punishes someone who hits a parent.

steps.title: Again: maybe the sword is harsher
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge comes back: maybe סייף is harsher than חנק, since the people of an עיר הנדחת get סייף and lose their property.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: the sword is more severe, since it is given to the people of a city led astray. And what makes it more severe? Their property is destroyed too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the עיר הנדחת challenge, this time against חנק. The answer comes right away in steps 12 and 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer from step 8 is not enough here by itself. It relied on the מדיח getting סקילה, which only proves that סקילה is harsher than סייף. The גמרא will reuse the מדיח argument (step 12), but it must add a source showing that the מדיח gets חנק (step 13).

keyTerms.meaning: Severity, the thing that makes something harsher

steps.confusionAlert: These words are the same as step 7, but now the target is חנק, not סקילה. The answer from step 8 only works here once we add a source that the מדיח gets חנק, which step 13 supplies.

phrases.english: On the contrary: the sword is more severe,
since it is given to the people of a city led astray.
And what is the severity?
Since their property is destroyed as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה: סַיִיף חָמוּר שֶׁכֵּן נִיתַּן לְאַנְשֵׁי עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ranking from step 10, using the same wording as step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חנק is harsher than סייף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The people of an עיר הנדחת get סייף and also lose their property, so סייף may be harsher than חנק.

steps.title: The one who leads astray sinned worse than those he misled
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the challenge: the מדיח's sin is greater than the sin of the people he led astray.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: whose wrongdoing is greater, the one who leads others astray, or the one who is led astray? You must say: the one who leads astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. It reuses the same reasoning it used back in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of the עיר הנדחת get סייף, and the מדיח who misled them sinned worse. So whatever death the מדיח gets must be harsher than סייף. This answer only works once we know which death the מדיח gets, and the next step supplies that.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the weight or seriousness of the sin
Greater
The one who was led astray
You must say (the obvious answer)

phrases.english: You can say: whose severity is greater,
that of the one who leads astray, or that of the one led astray?
You must say: that of the one who leads astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 using the same logic as step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing how serious the sinners are: the leader of the sin is worse than his followers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the people of the עיר הנדחת lose their property as well as getting סייף, סייף seems harsher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מדיח is worse than those he misled, so his death penalty is harsher than their סייף.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון gives the מדיח חנק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the רבנן say the מדיחים get סקילה, and רבי שמעון says חנק. So for רבי שמעון, חנק is harsher than סייף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: those who lead a city astray into idol worship get סקילה. רבי שמעון says: חנק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing which death the מדיח gets. This completes the answer from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim in step 10 that חנק is harsher than סייף matches רבי שמעון's view. He gives the מדיח חנק. Since the מדיח is worse than the people he led astray, who get סייף, חנק must be harsher than סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
Those who lead others astray (plural)
A city that was led into idol worship
Death by strangling

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון the מדיח gets חנק while the misled city gets סייף. So חנק is harsher than סייף.

phrases.english: And it was taught: the subverters of an idolatrous city are executed by stoning.
Rabbi Shimon says: by strangulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that finishes the answer begun in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that חנק is harsher than סייף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון rules that the מדיחים of an עיר הנדחת get חנק.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's favorite ברייתא about a betrothed girl
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: the רבנן give סקילה to a betrothed בת כהן who sinned, and to a betrothed girl who sinned with her father. רבי שמעון gives שריפה in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן often used to say: a betrothed נערה who is a בת כהן and committed adultery gets סקילה. רבי שמעון says: שריפה. If she sinned with her father, she gets סקילה. רבי שמעון says: שריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא that רבי יוחנן liked to quote. It shows the רבנן and רבי שמעון arguing between סקילה and שריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case could fit two death penalties. A betrothed נערה who sins gets סקילה, but a בת כהן who sins gets שריפה. A man's sin with his own daughter is also normally punished with שריפה. The רבנן choose סקילה and רבי שמעון chooses שריפה, and the next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a pearl in his mouth'; something he often used to say
A betrothed young girl
A כהן's daughter
Death by burning

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan was wont to say:

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁזִּינְּתָה – בִּסְקִילָה.
phrases.english: A betrothed young woman, daughter of a priest, who committed adultery: by stoning.
Rabbi Shimon says: by burning.
If she engaged in intercourse with her father: by stoning.
phrases.notes: This is any betrothed girl, not only a כהן's daughter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: by burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from comparing חנק and סייף to comparing סקילה and שריפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothed בת כהן who sinned, or betrothed girl who sinned with her father: סקילה according to the רבנן, שריפה according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What is this ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point the ברייתא is making.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what lesson the ברייתא is trying to teach. This sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings seem like plain rulings with no reason given. The גמרא wants to find the principle behind them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us?

phrases.english: What does this teach us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the ברייתא from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The new lesson behind the ברייתא's rulings.

steps.title: Who counts as the בת כהן who is burned
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן, only a married בת כהן gets שריפה. For רבי שמעון, both a betrothed and a married בת כהן get שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, the married woman was singled out for שריפה, not the betrothed one. According to רבי שמעון, both the betrothed and the married woman were singled out for שריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא teaches how far the special שריפה rule for a בת כהן reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives a sinning בת כהן שריפה. The רבנן limit this to a married woman, so a betrothed בת כהן keeps the regular betrothed girl's death, סקילה. רבי שמעון applies שריפה to both.

keyTerms.meaning: A married woman (after the חופה)
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before the חופה)
Was singled out for שריפה

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, the married one was singled out for burning,
and not the betrothed one.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – אַחַת אֲרוּסָה וְאַחַת נְשׂוּאָה
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, whether betrothed or married,
she is singled out for burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא teaches the scope of the בת כהן's שריפה: only a married one for the רבנן, both betrothed and married for רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The reason: which death is harsher
steps.stepSummary: The dispute depends on which death is harsher. The רבנן hold סקילה is harsher; רבי שמעון holds שריפה is harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason? Because according to the רבנן, סקילה is harsher, and according to רבי שמעון, שריפה is harsher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the dispute and answers it right away: each side ranks סקילה and שריפה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, a betrothed girl's סקילה is harsher. So she would not be 'moved up' to שריפה, which they see as lighter. The same reasoning applies to the girl who sinned with her father. For רבי שמעון, שריפה is the harsher death, so it wins in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the reason?
Harsher, more severe

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן hold סקילה is harsher than שריפה. רבי שמעון holds שריפה is harsher than סקילה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about how to read the בת כהן verse alone. Each side's ruling comes from how it ranks the two deaths.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
Because according to the Rabbis stoning is more severe,
while according to Rabbi Shimon burning is more severe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the positions laid out in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן rank סקילה above שריפה; רבי שמעון ranks שריפה above סקילה.

steps.title: Practical result: two death penalties
steps.stepSummary: The ranking also matters for someone who earned two court deaths, since he gets the harsher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference is for someone who was sentenced to two court deaths: he is judged with the harsher one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows another place where this ranking makes a real difference in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person committed two sins with different court deaths, he gets the harsher one. So if the two deaths are סקילה and שריפה, the רבנן give סקילה and רבי שמעון gives שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that comes out of it
Death penalties given by the court
He is judged with the harsher one

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the whole סוגיא works so hard to rank the four deaths. The order decides what happens to someone guilty of two capital sins.

phrases.english: The practical difference is for one who was sentenced to
two court-imposed death penalties,
he is punished with the more severe one.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ לְמִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּיב שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the ranking given in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Someone who earns two court deaths gets the harsher one, so the רבנן and רבי שמעון disagree in practice whenever סקילה and שריפה meet.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning and source behind רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון gets his view that שריפה is harsher, so that even a betrothed בת כהן gets שריפה. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 we learned that the whole argument depends on which death is harsher. Now the גמרא wants to see how רבי שמעון proves that שריפה is the harsher one.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (Here it means: what is the reason or source?)

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Shimon's reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining that the argument depends on which death is harsher, the גמרא asks for רבי שמעון's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי שמעון's view that שריפה is harsher than סקילה and applies to a betrothed בת כהן.

steps.title: A ברייתא: two general rules
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון: the Torah states two general rules that relate to a בת כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says, two general rules were stated about a בת כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by quoting a ברייתא from רבי שמעון. He says the Torah gave two general rules about women who sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules are: a betrothed woman (ארוסה) who sins gets סקילה, and a married woman (נשואה) who sins gets חנק. רבי שמעון is about to show that the בת כהן is an exception to both rules.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
General rules (singular: כְּלָל)
The daughter of a כהן

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says,
Two general rules were stated regarding a daughter of a kohen.
phrases.notes: The two rules: a betrothed woman who sins gets stoning, and a married woman who sins gets strangling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון's source is a ברייתא built on the two general rules for a betrothed woman and a married woman.

steps.title: Only a בת כהן, not a בת ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops the ברייתא and asks: aren't these two rules true for every Jewish woman, not just a בת כהן?
steps.simpleTranslation: With a בת כהן and not with a בת ישראל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts the ברייתא because its wording seems wrong. The two general rules apply to every woman, so why does it say they were stated about a בת כהן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: סקילה for an ארוסה and חנק for a נשואה are the normal rules for any Jewish woman, including a בת ישראל. Saying they were stated 'regarding a בת כהן' makes it sound like they are only about her, which cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish woman who is not from a כהן family

phrases.english: Regarding a daughter of a kohen, and not regarding a daughter of a Yisrael?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'בבת כהן' in רבי שמעון's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rules of סקילה for an ארוסה and חנק for a נשואה apply to all women, so they cannot be limited to a בת כהן.

steps.title: Read it as: also with a בת כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the rules apply to everyone, and also to a בת כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: also with a בת כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one word in the ברייתא. It means: these two rules apply to every woman, and also to a בת כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a בת כהן starts out in the same two groups as everyone else, betrothed or married. That matters because in the next line the Torah 'pulls her out' of those groups, and you can only be pulled out of a group you were in.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)

phrases.english: Say: also regarding a daughter of a kohen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by fixing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the two rules apply only to a בת כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rules apply to all women, and a בת כהן is included in them too.

steps.title: The Torah pulls the בת כהן out of both groups
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the פסוק about a בת כהן takes the married one out of the married group and the betrothed one out of the betrothed group.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק took the married woman out of the group of married women, and the betrothed woman out of the group of betrothed women.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on. The פסוק that gives a בת כהן שריפה applies to both a married and a betrothed בת כהן, so it pulls each of them out of her normal group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a נשואה gets חנק and an ארוסה gets סקילה. רבי שמעון reads the בת כהן פסוק as covering both, so both are moved to שריפה. This is his view from step 16; the רבנן there apply the פסוק only to a married בת כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק took out (made an exception)
A fully married woman
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before the wedding)
Strangling, the normal death for a married woman who sins

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the בת כהן is no longer counted as a married or betrothed woman. She still is. The פסוק only changes which death she gets.

phrases.english: And the verse took out a married woman from the general rule of a married woman,
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 21:9: a בת כהן who sins 'shall be burned with fire.'

phrases.english: and a betrothed woman from the general rule of a betrothed woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side point about the wording, the ברייתא continues building רבי שמעון's proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בת כהן פסוק makes an exception for both a married and a betrothed בת כהן and moves both to שריפה.

steps.title: Both exceptions make the punishment harsher
steps.stepSummary: Just as moving the married בת כהן was meant to make it harsher, moving the betrothed בת כהן was also meant to make it harsher. So שריפה is harsher than סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as when the פסוק took the married woman out of the married group it was to be stricter, so too when the פסוק took the betrothed woman out of the betrothed group it was to be stricter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his proof. Both exceptions in the same פסוק must point the same way, toward a harsher punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the married בת כהן, the change from חנק to שריפה is clearly harsher, since שריפה ranks above חנק. The same פסוק moves the betrothed בת כהן from סקילה to שריפה, so that must be harsher too. That proves שריפה is harsher than סקילה, which is רבי שמעון's view from step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: To be stricter, to make the punishment harsher
Just as... so too... (a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's proof: one פסוק pulls the בת כהן out of two groups. Out of the married group, the change is clearly harsher (חנק to שריפה). So out of the betrothed group it must also be harsher (סקילה to שריפה). That means שריפה is harsher than סקילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ranking decides the case of someone who earned two court deaths, from step 18. By רבי שמעון's ranking, שריפה counts as harsher than סקילה.

phrases.aramaic: מָה כְּשֶׁהוֹצִיא הַכָּתוּב נְשׂוּאָה מִכְּלַל נְשׂוּאָה לְהַחְמִיר,
phrases.english: Just as when the verse took out a married woman from the general rule of a married woman, it was to be stricter,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כְּשֶׁהוֹצִיא הַכָּתוּב אֲרוּסָה מִכְּלַל אֲרוּסָה לְהַחֲמִיר.
phrases.english: so too when the verse took out a betrothed woman from the general rule of a betrothed woman, it was to be stricter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה כְּשֶׁהוֹצִיא הַכָּתוּב נְשׂוּאָה מִכְּלַל נְשׂוּאָה לְהַחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the two exceptions just described.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי שמעון, שריפה is harsher than סקילה, because the פסוק that moves a betrothed בת כהן from סקילה to שריפה must be making her punishment harsher, just as it does for a married בת כהן.

steps.title: The false witnesses against a בת כהן are punished like those against any woman
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: the עדים זוממין against a married or betrothed בת כהן get the same punishment as the עדים זוממין against a regular Jewish woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Witnesses who were caught lying about a married בת כהן are judged together with liars about a married regular Jewish woman. Witnesses caught lying about a betrothed בת כהן are judged together with liars about a betrothed regular Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון finishes with one more rule. It is about lying witnesses (עדים זוממין) who falsely accused a בת כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת כהן herself was moved into a harsher group and gets שריפה. Her lying witnesses do not move with her. They stay in the regular groups: חנק for lying about a married woman, and סקילה for lying about a betrothed woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who were proven to have testified falsely. They get the punishment they tried to cause.
A fully married woman
A betrothed woman (after קידושין but before נישואין)
Included in, part of the same group as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the lying witnesses get שריפה just because the בת כהן would have gotten שריפה. The ברייתא says the opposite: they are punished like witnesses against any regular woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: The bigger punishment belongs only to the בת כהן herself. It does not spread to the people who falsely accused her.

phrases.english: The lying witnesses against a married daughter of a כהן
are included with the lying witnesses against a married daughter of a regular Jew;
and the lying witnesses against a betrothed daughter of a כהן
are included with the lying witnesses against a betrothed daughter of a regular Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוממי נשואה בת כהן בכלל זוממי נשואה בת ישראל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same ברייתא of רבי שמעון by adding a rule about the witnesses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The harsher punishment of the בת כהן does not pass to her lying witnesses. They are punished like witnesses against a regular woman.

steps.title: Does 'תחל' include a בת כהן who broke שבת?
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא quotes the פסוק about a בת כהן and asks whether the word 'תחל' (profanes) could include breaking שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And the daughter of a כהן, when she profanes herself...' Maybe this means even if she profaned שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that reads the בת כהן פסוק word by word. This step only raises the possibility; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תחל' comes from the same root as 'חילול שבת'. So one could think any kind of 'profaning', even breaking שבת, would make a בת כהן get שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. This opens a ברייתא.
She profanes, she makes herself unholy
One might think. It raises a possible reading that will be tested.
She broke שבת

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'And the daughter of a כהן, when she profanes herself'
One might think: even if she profaned שבת?
phrases.notes: 'תחל' and 'חללה' share the same root. That is why this idea comes up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא that explains the same פסוק of בת כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא raises the possibility that any 'profaning', even breaking שבת, could be included in the פסוק.

steps.title: The word 'לזנות' limits it to sins of זנות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the פסוק says 'לזנות', so it only means profaning through forbidden relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'by acting promiscuously.' The פסוק is talking about profaning through forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from the last step by pointing to the next word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full phrase is 'כי תחל לזנות'. The word 'לזנות' tells us what kind of profaning is meant. So breaking שבת is not included.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us (by saying...)
To act promiscuously, to sin with forbidden relations
Kinds of profaning

phrases.english: The פסוק says: 'by acting promiscuously'
The פסוק is speaking about profaning through promiscuity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'לזנות' limits 'תחל' to sins of forbidden relations, not breaking שבת.

steps.title: Does it include an unmarried בת כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether an unmarried בת כהן who sinned would also get שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: even if she is unmarried?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the פסוק is about זנות, the ברייתא asks whether it covers an unmarried woman too. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לזנות' alone does not say whether she must be married. So one could think any בת כהן who sinned with a man gets שריפה, even if she is single.

keyTerms.meaning: An unmarried woman, not tied to any husband

phrases.english: One might think: even if she is unmarried?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 27 and asks how wide the word 'לזנות' reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the שריפה of a בת כהן apply even when she is unmarried?

steps.title: A גזרה שוה on 'אביה' shows she must be tied to a husband
steps.stepSummary: Both our פסוק and the פסוק about a betrothed woman who sinned use the word 'אביה'. Just as that one is about a woman tied to a husband, this one is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here the פסוק says 'her father', and there the פסוק says 'her father'. There it means זנות while she is tied to a husband. So here too, it means זנות while she is tied to a husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers 'no' to the unmarried case by linking two פסוקים that share the word 'אביה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים about the betrothed girl who sinned 'in her father's house' is clearly about a woman tied to a husband. The shared word 'אביה' carries that condition over to the בת כהן. So an unmarried בת כהן does not get שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her father. This is the shared word that links the two פסוקים.
Here / there. Used to compare two פסוקים in a גזרה שוה.
A tie to a husband, whether through אירוסין or נישואין

steps.whatToRemember: A בת כהן gets שריפה only if she sinned while tied to a husband, meaning betrothed or married. An unmarried בת כהן is not included.

phrases.english: It says here 'her father,'
phrases.notes: Our פסוק goes on: 'את אביה היא מחללת', she profanes her father.

phrases.english: and it says there 'her father.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן זְנוּת עִם זִיקַת הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: Just as there it is promiscuity while tied to a husband,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן זְנוּת עִם זִיקַת הַבַּעַל.
phrases.english: so too here it is promiscuity while tied to a husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: נאמר כאן אביה ונאמר להלן אביה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 using a גזרה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through the shared word 'אביה', the law is limited to a בת כהן who is tied to a husband.

steps.title: Maybe 'אביה' means the sin must be with her father
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a different reading: perhaps 'אביה' comes to say she gets שריפה only if the sin was with her own father, and not with any other man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the פסוק says 'her father' only to leave out every other man?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own use of 'אביה' with another possible meaning of the word. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אביה' were about who she sinned with, the פסוק would cover only a sin with her father. Then the word would not be free for the גזרה שוה, and the law would become very narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it only says... It offers another way to read the פסוק.
To leave out, to exclude

phrases.english: Or perhaps it says 'her father'
only to leave out every other man?

steps.triggerLanguage: או אינו אומר אביה אלא להוציא את כל האדם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'אביה' used in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the word 'אביה' for the גזרה שוה in step 29
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אביה' may simply name the man she sinned with. That would limit the law to her father and leave the word unavailable for the גזרה שוה.

steps.title: 'היא מחללת' shows that any man is included
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'she profanes' her father. So it is her sin, with any man, that shames her father. 'אביה' does not limit the law to sins with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says 'she profanes', every man is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge from the last step and closes this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'את אביה היא מחללת' mean that she brings shame on her father through her sin. Her father is the one who is shamed, not the man she sinned with. So the sin can be with any man, and 'אביה' stays free for the גזרה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: She profanes, meaning she brings shame on her father
Every man is included

steps.whatToRemember: A betrothed or married בת כהן who sins with any man gets שריפה. Breaking שבת is not included, and an unmarried woman is not included.

phrases.english: When it says 'she profanes,'
phrases.notes: She is the one who shames her father, so he is not the man she sinned with.

phrases.english: then every man is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: כשהוא אומר היא מחללת הוי כל אדם אמור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading another phrase of the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אביה' names the man she sinned with, so only a sin with her father counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'היא מחללת' shows that she shames her father through a sin with any man. So all men are included.

steps.title: So what does the word 'her father' teach?
steps.stepSummary: Since 'אביה' does not limit the law to sins with her father, the ברייתא asks what the word is there for.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what do I do with the word 'her father'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא just ruled out reading 'אביה' as 'only with her father.' Now it asks what the word does teach, which sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the פסוק must teach something. Once the narrow reading of step 30 is rejected, 'אביה' needs a new job. This question brings the ברייתא back to the גזרה שוה from step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I fulfill (explain) this word? What is it teaching?
Her father, the key word in the פסוק

phrases.english: Then how do I explain 'her father'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the תירוץ in step 31: if 'אביה' isn't limiting, what is it for?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the word 'אביה' in the פסוק

steps.title: 'Her father' links to the betrothed woman: only a woman tied to a husband
steps.stepSummary: 'אביה' is used for a גזרה שוה with the betrothed woman who sinned, teaching that שריפה applies only to a בת כהן tied to a husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'her father,' and there it says 'her father.' Just as there it is about sinning while tied to a husband, here too it is about sinning while tied to a husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: 'אביה' is there to build the word-link (גזרה שוה) with the פסוק about the betrothed woman. That is why it is not wasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the reasoning of step 29, now as the reason the word 'אביה' is needed. Since the word is busy teaching the link, it cannot also mean 'only with her father.' The result is that an unmarried בת כהן is not included in שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: It says here... and it says there; the opening of a word-link between two פסוקים
Learning one law from another because both use the same word
Forbidden relations
A bond to a husband (betrothed or married)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'אביה' teaches, through a גזרה שוה, that the שריפה of a בת כהן applies only when she is tied to a husband.

phrases.english: Here it says 'her father,'
and there it says 'her father.'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:21, about the betrothed girl who sinned.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן זְנוּת עִם זִיקַת הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: Just as there it is forbidden relations while tied to a husband,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן זְנוּת עִם זִיקַת הַבַּעַל.
phrases.english: so too here it is forbidden relations while tied to a husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32 by restating the גזרה שוה of step 29 as the purpose of 'אביה'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אביה' is needed for the גזרה שוה, which limits the law to a woman with זיקת הבעל.

steps.title: Does the comparison also limit it to a young betrothed girl?
steps.stepSummary: If we learn from the betrothed girl, maybe the law is limited to a נערה who is ארוסה. Where would we learn the other cases?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe: just as there it is a young girl who is betrothed, here too it is only a young girl who is betrothed? Then a young girl who is married, an older girl who is betrothed, an older girl who is married, or even one who has grown old: where do we learn those?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own comparison. If we copy the betrothed-girl case, maybe we must copy all its details too, and then many women would be left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים is about a נערה who is ארוסה. A full comparison might limit our law to that exact case. The ברייתא lists every other case (married, בוגרת, elderly) and asks for a source to include them.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl in the first stage of maturity
A grown woman, past the stage of נערה
Betrothed (first stage of marriage)
Fully married
She has grown old
From where do we know?

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying these women are exempt. It is asking for a source to include them, since the comparison alone might seem to limit the law.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן נַעֲרָה וְהִיא אֲרוּסָה,
phrases.english: If so, just as there it is a young girl who is betrothed,
so too here only a young girl who is betrothed?
A young girl who is married,
a grown woman who is betrothed,
a grown woman who is married,
and even if she grew old: from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן נַעֲרָה וְהִיא אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the גזרה שוה of step 33 should be taken.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזרה שוה linking בת כהן to the betrothed נערה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison carries over, it may carry over every detail (נערה, ארוסה), leaving out married, grown, and elderly women.

steps.title: 'And the daughter of a כהן' includes every case
steps.stepSummary: The extra 'ו' in 'ובת כהן' teaches that the law applies in every case, not only to a betrothed נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And the daughter of a כהן': in every case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge. The word 'and' at the start of the פסוק widens the law to every בת כהן tied to a husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזרה שוה only teaches the need for זיקת הבעל. It does not carry over the age or the betrothed-only detail. The extra 'ו' adds the married, the בוגרת, and even the elderly woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches by saying...
And the daughter; the extra 'ו' is what widens the law
In any case, without limits

steps.whatToRemember: A בת כהן tied to a husband gets שריפה at any age and stage, whether betrothed or married, young or old.

phrases.english: The פסוק says: 'And the daughter of a כהן'
phrases.notes: The point is the extra 'ו' (and) at the start of the word.

phrases.english: in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 34 by finding an including word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra letter in the פסוק widens the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזרה שוה limits the law to a betrothed נערה, like the case in דברים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'ו' of 'ובת' includes every woman with זיקת הבעל, at any age.

steps.title: Quoting 'daughter of a כהן' for the next teaching
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes the words 'בת כהן' to begin a new teaching about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The daughter of a כהן.'

steps.deeperAnalysis: After using the 'ו' of 'ובת', the ברייתא now turns to the words 'בת כהן' themselves. On its own this line has no ruling yet. It just marks which words will be explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a כהן

phrases.english: 'The daughter of a כהן,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the דרשה on the 'ו', the ברייתא moves to the next words of the פסוק.
